shots.intent: Strong opening: establish the body-as-car-dashboard metaphor instantly.
shots.label_requirements: No medical claim label. Large amber dashboard icon; car interior should feel tasteful, not literal anatomy.
shots.visual_reason: A clean illustrated dashboard appears with normal gauges, inviting viewers into the metaphor before the awkward reveal.

shots.intent: Deliver the awkward-location punchline without depicting a patient.
shots.label_requirements: Use a generic dashboard light icon positioned over a fully clothed trouser-pocket silhouette; no nudity or anatomy.
shots.visual_reason: The warning icon migrates from the dashboard to an absurdly inconvenient place on a generic clothed silhouette.

shots.intent: Visualize denial as an obviously bad automotive repair.
shots.label_requirements: Single focal object: amber warning light covered by an oversized strip of silver duct tape.
shots.visual_reason: The presenter-equivalent response is comically incompetent: tape over the alert rather than inspect the cause.

shots.intent: Make the wellness-product pile-up feel ridiculous rather than aspirational.
shots.label_requirements: Illustrated product pile with fictional labels only; avoid real brands and medical-treatment claims.
shots.visual_reason: A tiny taped-over dashboard light is dwarfed by a towering pile of neon supplement jars.

shots.intent: Land the ‘confidence-branded moon dust’ joke as a visual payoff.
shots.label_requirements: One glittery faux supplement sachet, floating in space with a tiny confidence flag; fictional packaging.
shots.visual_reason: An absurd space-age sachet treats confidence like a commodity while the actual warning light remains ignored in the corner.

shots.intent: Reveal the relevant physical mechanism simply and accurately.
shots.label_requirements: Educational illustration, not anatomical realism: one red flow line moving through a simplified vascular pathway.
shots.source_label: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, 2024
shots.visual_reason: A single clear red flow line connects a heart-shaped pump icon to a simplified vascular network, supporting the statement that erections partly depend on blood flow.

shots.intent: Present the supported association without generalizing an older cohort's numerical effect size to younger viewers.
shots.label_requirements: Association, not diagnosis. Cite Uddin et al. 2018 and NIH; no numerical personal-risk estimate.
shots.visual_reason: An amber warning icon alongside a heart communicates a reason to review cardiovascular risk, without presenting a causal arrow or numerical prediction.

shots.intent: Translate the evidence into the script’s practical takeaway.
shots.label_requirements: Use ‘risk cue,’ not ‘diagnosis’ or ‘cause.’ Pair a small amber warning icon with a heart icon.
shots.visual_reason: The warning light transforms into a calm checklist icon beside a heart, reframing the issue from performance panic to risk review.

shots.intent: Show multiple possible contributors without pretending to identify an individual cause.
shots.label_requirements: Five evenly weighted icon tiles: stress cloud, anxious scribble, medication bottle, glucose droplet, vessel line. No tile visually dominates.
shots.source_label: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, 2024
shots.visual_reason: A tidy five-part contributor wheel gives each possibility equal visual weight, reinforcing that persistent ED has many causes.

shots.intent: Create a clear boundary against overdiagnosis.
shots.label_requirements: Big stamped word ‘NOT’ over a heart-disease diagnosis form; no alarming imagery.
shots.visual_reason: A bold NOT stamp lands on a mock diagnostic conclusion, making the non-diagnostic boundary unmistakable.

shots.intent: Reframe the symptom as a prompt for a normal conversation.
shots.label_requirements: A friendly clinician-office doorway with a small dashboard-warning icon becoming a speech bubble.
shots.source_label: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, 2024
shots.visual_reason: The amber warning light becomes a conversation bubble as it moves toward a clinician-office doorway.

shots.intent: Mock amateur online diagnosis, aimed at the situation and presenter behavior.
shots.label_requirements: Over-caffeinated corkboard detective scene with red yarn connecting supplement jar, magnifying glass, and dashboard light; no patient imagery.
shots.screen_text: STEP AWAY FROM THE RED YARN
shots.visual_reason: A melodramatic conspiracy-board investigation makes self-diagnosis look less competent than basic maintenance.

shots.intent: Present the practical maintenance list as the competent alternative.
shots.label_requirements: Five large checklist rows with simple icons. Keep all items legible at square size.
shots.visual_reason: The detective board snaps into an orderly five-item maintenance checklist: blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, medications, and stress.

shots.intent: Make ‘boring grown-up maintenance’ feel quietly heroic.
shots.label_requirements: Single focal image: mechanic-style checklist on a refrigerator, with a tiny cape clipped to it.
shots.visual_reason: The maintenance list receives an overly dramatic little cape, gently elevating mundane health follow-through into the real hero move.

shots.intent: Clarify the dashboard metaphor’s final distinction.
shots.label_requirements: Split illustration: left engine running normally; right amber warning light lit. No damage imagery.
shots.visual_reason: The engine hums calmly while the dashboard icon glows, visually separating a warning from a verdict.

shots.intent: Close with a visual callback to the taped warning light and the thesis.
shots.label_requirements: Return to sh03 dashboard. The duct tape peels itself off and becomes a neat maintenance checklist.
shots.visual_reason: The original tape-over-the-light joke resolves: the tape peels away, the warning becomes visible, and a sensible maintenance checklist replaces the moon-dust clutter.
